name: biogears_thermal
description: The BioGears temperature circuit (core and skin segments joined to clothing, enclosure and ambient air) in the real engine: core and skin temperatures, sweat, metabolic rate, heat-loss rates and per-compartment temperatures and heat flows, driven by the environment and by active heating, cooling or an applied temperature.

state_file.description: BioGears state in <runtime>/states or the package's states/ (or an absolute path)

patient_file.description: Patient file in <runtime>/patients (or a path), stabilized once (about 40 s) and then cached; replaces state_file

conditions.description: Chronic conditions applied while the patient stabilizes, e.g. {ChronicAnemia: {ReductionFactor: 0.3}}; with no patient_file, StandardMale.xml. A different patient, not a perturbation

patient_table.description: A Patients.csv (BioGears' template layout, one column per patient); with patient, the patient is generated from it, stabilized once and cached; replaces state_file

patient.description: The Name of a patient in patient_table

substance_table.description: A Substances.csv, or a folder with Substances.csv and/or Compounds.csv (BioGears' template layout): their substances and compounds are added to the engine's substances

circuit_additions.description: New path name -> {source, target, resistance_mmHg_s_per_mL}: a resistance path between two FullCardiovascular nodes in different vascular compartments, added with its compartment link so substances follow. A perturbation: the body responds over time

interval.description: Seconds per update; 0.02 (BioGears' timestep) resolves per-beat/per-breath waveforms. A non-binary-exact interval can lose the final update of a run to float time accumulation.

ambient_temperature_C.description: Air temperature around the body (not the air breathed; see respiration_ambient_temperature_C)

mean_radiant_temperature_C.description: Mean radiant temperature of the surroundings

respiration_ambient_temperature_C.description: Temperature of the air breathed; drives respiration heat loss

clothing_resistance_clo.description: Clothing thermal resistance (1 clo = 0.155 m^2 K/W)

active_heating_W.description: Active heating power; BioGears delivers power x area fraction

active_heating_area_fraction.description: Fraction of skin area under active heating, in (0, 1]

active_cooling_W.description: Active cooling power; BioGears removes power x area fraction

active_cooling_area_fraction.description: Fraction of skin area under active cooling, in (0, 1]

applied_temperature_on.description: 1 = apply applied_temperature_C over the clothing, 0 = off

applied_temperature_area_fraction.description: Fraction in (0, 1] by which BioGears blends the applied temperature with the ambient temperature

biogears.doc:
Bridge to one real BioGears 8.2.0 engine, exposing the selected modules (every BioGears
system is simulated every step; a module chooses only which readings and setpoints are ports).

``config.modules`` names entries of ``viva_biogears.modules.MODULES``. Each module
contributes a port subtree named after it:

- outputs: the module's BioGears data requests as ``overwrite[float]`` ports at the
  module's nested paths (e.g. ``cardiovascular/central/aorta/pressure_mmHg``);
- inputs, under the single ``setpoints`` port: the module's setpoints as
  ``overwrite[float]`` ports whose schema default is the baseline value, sent to
  BioGears as actions only on change (e.g. ``setpoints/cardiovascular/hemorrhage_rate_mL_per_min``).

Inputs and outputs use disjoint top-level port names on purpose: process-bigraph
projects ``initial_state()`` through the input wires as well as the output wires,
so a shared name would copy readings into the setpoint store.

Outputs follow ``BioGearsProcess``'s contract: ``initial_state()`` seeds each store
with the loaded state's reading and every update emits BioGears' current reading.
``irreversible_state`` turns True once BioGears reports its irreversible state; the
engine is not advanced after that. Identical requests from different modules share
one BioGears request. A request BioGears does not connect raises at load; a NaN
reading raises, naming the request, unless the request allows it.

All changed setpoint groups are validated before any action is sent, and so is the
airway rule: at most one module's ``airway_device`` connected, and none connecting
in the update in which another disconnects (BioGears would process the new device
before the old one's removal and fail every step).

The engine loads ``state_file`` (a name in ``<runtime>/states`` or the package's
``states/``, or an absolute path), or ``patient_file``/``conditions`` stabilized and
cached (``viva_biogears.patients``). A state saved mid-run carries its actions; each
setpoint group starts at the state's values (``ActionBinding.loaded``), so a branch
with the same setpoints continues the run exactly and one that differs sends the
change. A state whose airway is held by a device the process doesn't control is
refused when the process can connect one. ``save_state_times_s`` saves the engine
at those times (``viva_biogears.states``).

_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
